raw_response:
My land is about 8 mu, all flat. My father grew wheat and corn here, I grow wheat and corn here, my son will probably grow wheat and corn here. That's just how it is in Quzhou. The rotation is fixed in my head: winter wheat goes in around October, I harvest it in June, then I turn around and plant summer corn on the same ground, harvest that in September or October. Two crops a year, same fields, every year.

For wheat seed, I'll go to the village supply co-op and buy Jimai 22 or whatever improved variety they have this year — not the old stuff my grandfather saved, those yields are too low. For corn, I'll buy hybrid seed. Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever the shop recommends. Hybrid corn just outyields the old varieties too much to ignore.

Fertilizer: I apply compound fertilizer as base when I plant, then top-dress with urea at jointing for wheat, and at the big bell stage for corn. I know some people are cutting back on fertilizer but I'd rather not risk the yield — I need to sell enough to cover costs and have something left.

Water worries me every year. The water table keeps dropping and the electricity for pumping costs more than it used to. For wheat I'll irrigate three times — at sowing, jointing, and heading. For corn, twice should do unless it gets very dry.

Pesticide: two sprays for wheat (herbicide in spring, fungicide if there's rust), two for corn (herbicide early, something for borer if I see it).

After corn harvest I'll do rotary tillage to prep for wheat. After wheat harvest I'll go straight to no-till corn seeding — saves time and I need to get the corn in fast.
